title: DDIA 第 2 章 · 数据模型与查询语言 — 专业书籍精读 Book 2

questions.question: 关系模型当年战胜层次模型和网状模型，真正的胜利在哪里？
options: 把访问路径交给查询优化器自动决定，不再由程序员亲手写死
用写时模式强制校验结构，从根本上保证了字段质量和一致性
平铺的行列结构在磁盘上比指针更紧凑，存取效率因此大幅提高
用外键和规范化消除了数据冗余，修改一处就能做到全局生效
questions.explanation: 层次和网状时代要程序员沿访问路径一步步爬，改个查询就得重写一片代码；Codd 之后，你只描述要什么，怎么走由数据库自己决定，这也是声明式能持续优化、能并行的根。规范化确实是关系模型的好处，但它不是终结「指针丛林」的那一刀。
questions.question_en: When the relational model beat the hierarchical and network models, where did its real victory lie?
options_en: It let a query optimizer choose access paths automatically, so programmers no longer hard-coded them
It enforced structure through schema-on-write, fundamentally guaranteeing field quality and consistency
Flat rows and columns packed more compactly on disk than pointers, greatly improving access efficiency
Foreign keys and normalization eliminated redundancy, so a change in one place took effect everywhere
questions.explanation_en: In the hierarchical and network era, programmers had to crawl along access paths step by step, and changing a query meant rewriting swaths of code. After Codd, you describe only what you want and the database decides how to get there, which is also the root of why declarative queries can keep getting optimized and run in parallel. Normalization is indeed a benefit of the relational model, but it isn't the blow that ended the "jungle of pointers."

questions.question: 为什么说今天的文档数据库像是 1970 年代 IBM IMS 的「转世」？
options: 它们都把数据组织成一棵嵌套的树，也都对多对多关系束手无策
它们都把声明式查询交给优化器，只是优化器的成熟程度有所差别
它们都用读时模式解释数据，字段错配的问题都会拖到读取时才暴露
它们都靠手工维护的指针连接记录，查询要沿预设路径一步步爬
questions.explanation: IMS 的层次模型就是一棵大树，和 JSON 文档惊人地像，同样处理不好多对多，历史是螺旋而不是直线。手工指针和沿路径爬取说的是它的对手、网状模型 CODASYL，这是最容易混淆的一项。
questions.question_en: Why can today's document databases be described as a "reincarnation" of IBM's IMS from the 1970s?
options_en: Both organize data as one nested tree, and both are helpless with many-to-many relationships
Both leave declarative queries to an optimizer, differing only in how mature that optimizer is
Both interpret data with schema-on-read, so mismatched fields only surface at read time
Both link records with hand-maintained pointers, so queries crawl step by step along preset paths
questions.explanation_en: IMS's hierarchical model was one big tree, uncannily like a JSON document, and it handled many-to-many just as poorly: history is a spiral, not a straight line. Hand-maintained pointers and crawling along paths describe its rival, the CODASYL network model, which makes this the easiest option to confuse.
